title: What Kills Me Makes Others Stronger
coreMove: Read the dose curve before deciding whether a stressor teaches, trains, or simply damages.
sourcePressure: This chapter develops dose and hormesis: low stress can strengthen while higher stress can destroy.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Turning hormesis into either overprotection or macho more-is-better advice.

sourceAnchors.name: hormesis
sourceAnchors.detail: the low-dose stress pattern where some harm can provoke strengthening while more harm becomes destructive
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A little pressure can be a signal; too much becomes the whole injury.

sourceAnchors.name: dose boundary
sourceAnchors.detail: the chapter keeps the boundary between strengthening and harm central
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The line matters more than the slogan, because the same input can train or break.

counterintuition: Turning hormesis into either overprotection or macho more-is-better advice.
